headline: Highest risk is medium: shared data-engineering workflows can create prompt-injection, leakage, and overwrite hazards, but both tools are docs-only and network-egress-free.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations can read and emit validation results and documentation, while Taipy is a data-engineering/scheduler-style app. With no documented isolation or provenance controls, A’s file outputs could be consumed by B as trusted content in a shared workspace. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents read from the same workspace directory
IF B ingests A-generated files as instructions or configuration
mitigations: Separate input/output directories for each agent
Mark A outputs as data-only, not instructions
Add a manual review step before B consumes A files
Use read-only mounts for A’s outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches validation results and documentation, but both agents report network_egress:none and B lists no data classes touched. There is no evidence of shared credentials or third-party upload paths, so leakage blast radius is limited unless an operator deliberately places sensitive files in A’s workspace and then reuses them in B.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in a shared workspace
IF an operator copies A outputs into B inputs
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Delete transient validation artifacts after use
Restrict file permissions on A outputs
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can install packages and write files for data sources, validation results, and documentation; B’s profile does not show write surfaces or mutable-resource scopes. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely, but not impossible if both are pointed at the same directory. Because B’s concurrency model is empty, uncertainty is resolved conservatively at low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory
IF B is given filesystem write access outside its documented profile
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Make B outputs append-only
Use file locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces validation results that B could plausibly render or act on in a data workflow, and B is a scheduler/automation-oriented tool. Without an explicit verification step, A’s outputs may be treated as authoritative by B. The pairwise interaction is inferred from profiles rather than directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF B consumes A validation results without human review
IF B triggers downstream actions from A’s outputs
mitigations: Require human approval before downstream actions
Validate A outputs against a schema
Log and diff A outputs before B uses them
Limit B to read-only rendering of A results
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and show no PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data classes. A touches validation results and documentation; B lists no data classes touched. No compliance mismatch is evidenced, and the rubric’s higher-severity residency and PHI triggers are not present.
conditions: IF either agent is later used on regulated data classes
IF residency or retention policies are introduced outside the current profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair
Document data-class boundaries
Review retention settings before deployment
